previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and bilateral below-knee amputations was readmitted due to hypotension after her PICC line dislodged during outpatient ertapenem therapy for recent Klebsiella sepsis. She received IV fluids, which resolved her hypotension. During admission, she was found to have C. difficile infection and candiduria with persistent pyuria, prompting treatment with oral vancomycin and fluconazole. A CT urogram showed tiny non-obstructing kidney stones but no anatomic abnormalities. Her insulin regimen was optimized to prevent hypoglycemia, lisinopril was held due to hypotension risk, and metoprolol was reduced. She was discharged home with nursing services, stable and afebrile, on a 10-day course of vancomycin and 14-day course of fluconazole, with follow-up arranged for her wounds and primary care.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old woman with DM1, sCHF, h/o 
polysubstance abuse and NSTEMI, recent admission for Klebsiella 
UTI with subsequent sepsis, readmitted with C. Diff colitis and 
funguria, discharged on PO vanc and fluconazole on ___, now 
presenting with new hyperkalemia and ARF. Brief hospital course 
by problem:
.
# Acute renal failure: Likely multifactorial: pre-renal azotemia 
from poor PO intake, as well as the UTI, and perhaps AIN from 
Fluconazole (given urine eos). Cr was 2.2 on admission and 
improved after hydration and antibiotics. Cr had trended down to 
~1 upon discharge.
.
# Hyperkalemia: secondary to ARF. Potassium was 8.9 on 
admission, w/o EKG changes. She was treated with kayexalate, 
insulin, glucose, and IVF, and the potassium normalized. It was 
3.3 upon discharge.
.
# UTI: UA showed >1000 WBC with many bacteria. Considering the 
patient's recent UTI from klebsiella ESBL, we started her 
empirically on Meropenem. Urine culture later showed Citrobacter 
freundii sensitive to ciprofloxacin, so the meropenem was d/c'd 
and we started cipro, with a 14-day course planned. Last day of 
Cipro will be ___.  
.
# Recurrent UTIs: The patient is incontinent and has had 
numerous UTIs. Urology was consulted and a straight cath 
obtained 600cc urine, suggesting improper bladder evacuation. 
Her neurogenic voiding issues as well as fecal incontinence 
contribute to her UTIs.  She is being discharged with a foley, 
and will follow-up with ___ clinic on ___ for further workup 
and to learn clean intermittent cath.
.
# H/o C. diff colitis: No diarrhea during this admission. We 
continued the vancomycin for prophylaxis at a lowered dose (125 
mg PO Q6H) per ID's recommendation.  Will continue for 1 week 
after last Cipro dose (last dose will be ___.
.
# H/o funguria: No evidence of yeast on UA. Fluconazole was 
discontinued. 
.
# Right BKA wound: Patient went to OR for BKA revision on 
___, without complications.  The surgical site at the time of 
discharge is clean, without erythema or discharge.  She will 
follow up with Vascular Surgery.     
. 
# HTN: Poorly controlled, with SBP to 190s. We increased 
metoprolol succinate from 50mg to 75mg daily, then up to 100mg 
daily.  in addition, started lisinopril 5mg daily. Blood 
pressure was subsequently slightly better controlled but still 
not within goal (was 130-150 upon discharge).
.
# Diabetes: Blood sugars were not optimally controlled during 
this admission, due to inconsistent diet. We continued coverage 
with ISS.   
.
#Nausea, vomiting
Patient complained of nausea and vomiting for a few days before 
discharge, relieved by IV Compazine; this may have been related 
to pain med usage.  At the time of discharge, she had been able 
to tolerate PO diet all day without complaint.
.
# Neuropathy: Stable. Continued gabapentin, morphine for pain 
control per home regimen.  At teh time of discharge, she was at 
her baseline level of pain.

***Labs pending at the time of discharge: final blood culture 
result.***
